items.title: Show HN: Wienerdog – memory and self-improving skills for Claude Code/Codex
items.why_it_matters: Wienerdog is a zero-config tool that sets up a tailored CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md file in your repository by asking you a few quick questions. This gives Claude Code and Codex instant, accurate context about your project rules and stack without you having to manually write system prompts. Try running `npx wienerdog@latest init` in your AI-ingest folder today to instantly improve Claude's coding accuracy.

items.title: Show HN: Cockpit for you Claude Code agents in Rust
items.why_it_matters: Cockpit is a terminal dashboard designed specifically to organize and manage multiple Claude Code sessions, git branches, and project scripts in one clean interface. If you find yourself drowning in open terminal windows while vibe coding, this keeps your workspace organized. Try installing Cockpit this week to run and track your Next.js dev server and Claude Code sessions side-by-side.

items.title: Show HN: Copy any website pixel perfect
items.why_it_matters: This tool automates the process of copying UI designs by iteratively prompting Claude to refine code until it matches a target website perfectly, rather than letting the LLM guess dimensions. It is a great shortcut for building clean frontends without getting bogged down in CSS. Try running it against a landing page you like to generate a clean Next.js component you can drop straight into your project.

items.title: Show HN: DSCode – Coding Agent Powered by DeepSeek
items.why_it_matters: DSCode is a terminal-based coding agent powered by DeepSeek, offering a low-cost alternative to Claude Code for planning, editing, and testing code. Since you have previously seen massive cost savings by delegating tasks to DeepSeek, this gives you a dedicated CLI tool to do exactly that. Try installing `dscode` this week and use it to handle a simple refactoring task on your Supabase schema.

items.title: Show HN: An MCP server that knows what that error message means
items.why_it_matters: This MCP server scans source code to match error templates and instantly explains what they mean and how to fix them, acting like an automated Stack Overflow. Since Claude Code supports MCP, you can plug this directly into your workflow to stop wasting time deciphering cryptic build errors. Try adding this server to your Claude Code config today so it can auto-resolve the next Next.js or Supabase error you hit.
